721.quote_or_event: “One who does not frighten anyone, and who is not afraid of anyone else - says Nanak, listen, mind: call him spiritually wise.”
721.explanation: Guru Tegh Bahadur makes fearlessness, neither inspiring fear nor yielding to it, the mark of the truly wise (giani).
721.tie_back: The Kural says those who know the full range of words will not falter before a powerful gathering; Guru Tegh Bahadur says true wisdom is shown precisely by not being afraid of anyone.
721.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1427, Salok Mahalla 9 (salok 16), Guru Tegh Bahadur (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
721._accuracy_note: A strong fit linking wisdom and fearlessness, though the salok concerns fearlessness in all of life, not specifically speaking in an assembly.

722.quote_or_event: “The Siddhas formed an assembly; sitting in their Yogic postures, they shouted, ‘Salute this gathering of Saints.’ … I offer my salutation to the One who is true, infinite and incomparably beautiful.”
722.explanation: Siddh Gosht opens with Guru Nanak facing an assembly of learned yogis; he answers their questions one by one, setting out his teaching so that it reaches them.
722.tie_back: The Kural calls 'most learned of the learned' those who can set out their learning before the learned so that it reaches them; Siddh Gosht shows Guru Nanak doing this before the Siddhas' assembly.
722.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 938, Raag Ramkali, Siddh Gosht, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
722._accuracy_note: A strong fit for speaking before a learned assembly, though the dialogue aims at spiritual truth rather than at showing one's learning.

723.quote_or_event: “Nanak speaks the Word of Truth; he proclaims the Truth at this, the right time.”
723.explanation: This closes the Tilang hymn in which Guru Nanak openly describes the slaughter of Babur's invasion; Sikh tradition remembers him speaking the truth while armies raged.
723.tie_back: The Kural says many will die among enemies but few can stand fearless in an assembly; Guru Nanak's courage was to speak the truth openly in a time of terror.
723.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 723, Raag Tilang, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
723._accuracy_note: Strong on fearless speech, but it is truth spoken before violent power, not composure in a debating council, and the link to Babur rests on the hymn's content and tradition.

724.quote_or_event: “Let us form a partnership, and share our virtues; let us abandon our faults, and walk on the Path.”
724.explanation: Guru Nanak invites companions to pool their good qualities, each giving and receiving, and to leave their faults behind.
724.tie_back: The Kural says to give what one has learned to the learned and take from those who know more; Guru Nanak's partnership of virtues is the same two-way exchange.
724.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 766, Raag Suhi, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
724._accuracy_note: A good fit on mutual giving and taking, though Gurbani speaks of sharing virtues rather than scholarly knowledge.

725.quote_or_event: “Contemplate and reflect upon knowledge, and you will become a benefactor to others.”
725.explanation: Guru Nanak values learning that has been reflected on (vichar), because it equips a person to serve others.
725.tie_back: The Kural tells the student to learn the method of reasoning properly so as to answer fearlessly in assembly; Guru Nanak too asks for learning that is reflected on and put to use.
725.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 356, Raag Aasaa, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
725._accuracy_note: Next-best: both want disciplined, applied learning, but Gurbani's goal is benefiting others, not winning debates through logic.

726.quote_or_event: “If you desire to play this game of love with Me, then step onto My Path with your head in hand.”
726.explanation: Guru Nanak makes courage, being ready to give one's head, the entry condition for the path of love.
726.tie_back: The Kural asks what use a sword or books are to one without courage; Guru Nanak likewise says nothing on the path is of use without the courage to stake everything.
726.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1412, Salok Vaaran Thay Vadheek, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
726._accuracy_note: Reasonable but partial: courage is the shared point, but the verse is about devotional self-surrender, not about weapons or learning.

727.quote_or_event: “He alone is known as a spiritual hero, who fights in defense of religion. He may be cut apart, piece by piece, but he never leaves the field of battle.”
727.explanation: Bhagat Kabir defines the true hero as one who actually stands and fights for the right and never quits the field.
727.tie_back: The Kural pictures learning held by the fearful as a bright sword in the hand of one unfit to fight, never used; Kabir's hero is the opposite, one who uses his strength and stays on the field.
727.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1105, Raag Maru, Bhagat Kabir (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
727._accuracy_note: Reasonable contrast-parallel; Kabir's battle is largely inner or in defence of the weak, and he says nothing about learning.

728.quote_or_event: “You may read and read loads of books; you may read and study vast multitudes of books. … O Nanak, only one thing is of any account: everything else is useless babbling and idle talk in ego.”
728.explanation: In Asa ki Vaar, Guru Nanak says cartloads of reading count for nothing without the one thing that matters, the Name.
728.tie_back: The Kural says however many subjects one has studied, one is useless without the power to present good things to a good assembly; Guru Nanak too says vast reading alone is of no account.
728.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 467, Raag Aasaa, Asa ki Vaar (salok), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
728._accuracy_note: Next-best: both call vast learning useless without something more, but Gurbani's missing element is the Name, not skill in public speech.

729.quote_or_event: “That scholar who is full of greed, arrogant pride and egotism, is known to be a fool.”
729.explanation: Guru Nanak says a learned person ruled by greed and ego is to be counted a fool despite his learning.
729.tie_back: The Kural says the learned who dread a good assembly rank lower than the unlearned; Guru Nanak likewise says a scholar can be ranked among fools because of an inner failing.
729.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 140, Raag Maajh, Majh ki Vaar (salok), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
729._accuracy_note: Reasonable: the same 'learned yet a fool' verdict, but the failing Gurbani names is ego and greed, not timidity.

730.quote_or_event: “They alone are truly alive, whose minds are filled with the Lord. O Nanak, no one else is truly alive;”
730.explanation: Guru Nanak says that only those in whom the Lord dwells are really living; the rest only appear to be alive.
730.tie_back: The Kural says those who cannot pass on their learning for fear are like the dead though alive; Guru Nanak uses the same living-yet-dead contrast.
730.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 142, Raag Maajh, Majh ki Vaar (salok), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
730._accuracy_note: Next-best: the 'alive only in name' rhetoric is shared, but Gurbani's test of being alive is the Name, not sharing learning.
